title: The Eye as a Masterpiece of Divine Wisdom
english: While the Hebrews had our Lord and Savior, like a careful and wise physician, who does not employ another method of treatment for a first experience of a disease, he intends to heal a blind man who was found from birth, not having become blind through any fault or suffering, but by a defect of nature produced from the womb into life.

Having seen the man, he stood and was ready for healing, a healing superior to human speech and art. For medical speech imposes upon those diseases a theory—those things which, after nature has completed the animal and leads it toward light, happen in certain circumstances later—but when [the disease] is joined to the body, healing is not promised of a fault. Yet not even of all the sufferings that come about later.

And the maimed of men are witnesses to this, for no physician has repaired the loss of their limbs. Therefore also the disciples, having seen the suffering and seeing a man who had not tasted the best pleasure of light, were searching for the cause of the harm and were inquiring from the Lord, not very knowing, whether he was brought into life such as this because of his own sin or because of the faults of his parents (cf. John 9:2).

On both sides the question carries a consequence; for the child would not have been judged on account of the fathers, God not punishing one for another; nor indeed did he escape punishment for his own faults, if this one was born blind. For no one is a sinner before birth. Therefore the inquiry is not very proven; but so that we may learn how the truth, our Lord, responded to the question.

For this suffering, he says, 'O disciples, is not a retribution for sins, but a preparation for an upcoming economy, so that the man formerly considered common might act the things above man, and the Creator of all things, after the first creation, might find an occasion now to create, and through the particular might be made to trust the universal, and the hard and difficult people might be persuaded to worship, casting away the stones.'
Let the eyes that do not see be enlightened, so that the sun of righteousness (cf. Malachi 4:2) might shine upon the souls of the unwise.

Let a paradoxical thing be set forth and new sights be created, so that those who are in dispute may learn how the so-called son of Joseph, if he were truly a carpenter's boy, would have been able to mend a split plank, or gather together wood torn from harmony, or see a broken beam, or smooth the roughness of the boards, or do entirely those things which a craftsman father teaches his son according to the skill of the trade.

And a part of man, and the most beautiful part, the eye, which is most lovingly fashioned by nature, no one else could have made, unless he who has the authority of the first principle according to nature. Even if someone wishes to apply his mind closely to human limbs, in this very thing, the form of the body, he will behold the almighty and manifold wisdom of God in a small descriptive representation, such as the zeal of the art has demonstrated. For first, a certain grace is poured out upon it, and it is both most soft and incorporeal, as one might say, having the solid within the tender, and the arranged within the soft, and it is streaked with various colors.

Its center indeed has the description of black, and this is not a single-colored thing throughout, but connected with various circles; its center and middle having the deepest part, while the outer periphery is fading in color toward the more yellow part. Around this, the white has been draped from without, shining and lucid, not having a white that is unmixed, but having been made in a certain crystalline and beaming form. The red lies around the pupil, so that it may mix grace with the white and the black. Upon these things, it is thus lucid and smooth in its density, so that even those nearby make shapes like images, and like an accurate mirror, the characters of those being conversed with are impressed; for this reason also its middle circle, the center, is called a pupil, always showing a human form to the one looking opposite. For just as it is not possible for one looking into a mirror not to immediately shadow his own character upon the material, so it is not possible for the one standing as a representative of man not to engrave the familiar form upon the eye. When, indeed, men look at one another...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Power of the Siloam Washing
english: They become mirrors to one another. Therefore, the eye is worthy of wonder among the created things. For this also interprets God to me, accurately perceiving all of creation and, by pointing out the artisan through the working of things, it interprets the invisible to the soul from the visible; through this I have knowledge of the sun and the order of the heavens, and I have studied the beauty of the stars and the substance and nature of the earth, the difference of seeds and the variety of plants and the diverse coloring of hues, the depth of darkness and the shining of light, and all simply as much as God has created.

If an eye had not existed, creation would have been without witness, with no one seeing the wisdom and power of God being preserved within it. Because of this, therefore, this wonderful arrangement of the eyes, the eyes were also created by design, so that we might cast off the lowly ideas approaching us from the flesh concerning the Only-begotten, by the great work of things coming to be, casting out from the soul every lowly and vulgar conceit; let us know, however, that the blessed light and beauty of the divinity received an earthen vessel to serve us, like lamps, the shining light.

The Lord performs the healing himself, and he does not use word alone for the operation, having supported all through the command for the adornment; he healed the paralytic with two words; but he also heals the blindness now with mouth and hands and much other foresight, so that he might instill firm faith through things into the unbelieving.

He stoops upon the ground and works a clot with saliva, using the earth for this purpose toward the healing, so that he might show how from that clay, whence in the beginning the living creature was formed in its entirety, a complete part is being made from the remainder. With saliva he takes this up and joins together what was scattered and unattached, so that he might show us clearly that by the power of his mouth the Word set all things in order. For by the word the heavens were established (Ps 33:5), and by the spirit of his mouth all their power (Job 33:4).

Perhaps also because of this he heals by stooping, so that those about to insult a little later with spittle might be subdued by fear; and yet the insolence of the madmen did not cease, but he was spat upon much by the...

Such things are achieved through a fall. In this first act, the creative power is shown, and by the command to wash in the pool of Siloam, the salvation through water is demonstrated to us, which the one sent (Siloam) granted to all. For then we see well when we are cleansed by the mystical water; then the light of grace surrounds us, when the power of baptism washes away the stain of sins and the spots. And all who obey the command of Siloam see the spiritual light, which enlightens every man coming into the world. Oh, the wonder and the great energy!

The man, blind a moment ago, went out from the pool with his face adorned by the addition to his eyes, seeing accurately toward the solar ray. The matter astonished the neighbors and the acquaintances. The new manner of the healing disturbed his life; the man was surrounded by the city, seeing that the work was becoming known by all, new and paradoxical, by Jesus born in Bethlehem, that little infant who was laid in the manger among the rushes. For these are the things which caused the Jews to disbelieve in the divinity.

Not then, O foolish and hard-hearted ones, apply your reasoning to the men of the age. Beginning from Adam, investigate all the following, if you find what has happened now and has been done upon others, having a life that is a model of such a healing; and again, at the dragging away of my Lord, you bring forward the child of the carpenter, whose brothers you know, whose house you know. Count all the lowly things, contend, and pour out much of our dishonor. But if neither man has done anything of this kind, nor has life had such a story, having recognized your own ignorance, look back toward the truth. Wash also yourselves in the Siloam, so that you do not perish in blindness.

But nothing was as it should be regarding them. Neither a word instructed, nor a deed taught, nor the energy of wonders nourished; but on the contrary, through innate ignorance, they attempted in myriad ways to obscure and to drag away; and malice turned back upon them to the contrary. For as much as they disbelieved, and asking...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Inheritance of Unbelief
english: They strove to overturn it, for the truth was being made more certain by so much. And he suffered the same from the beasts as those, having been wounded by something and not yet having received the whole point in the stomach, with a rush and rivalry, concentrating all the iron upon itself.

7.8.1 First, meddlingness: if this same man, and not another in his place, was shown; this being clearly testified by the man, who cried out and clearly reported the sequence of the healing, that even the mud was used as a medicine for the blindness, and that the washing of the mud in the pool provided sight. These things the neighbors investigated and learned; the Pharisees sought and did not believe.

7.8.2 Second, a technique for the invalidation of what had happened was taken up, to try to show that Christ is not the one who worked the healing. Since the man cried out to the Savior and gave back the grace by his confession and his proclamation, and made public the benefactor, they, being prevented in their mouths, reeling in their opinion, having nothing what to do, 7.8.3 run back again to the inquiry of the passion, and whether he was blind from birth; they investigate this and search the parents of the man, becoming precise examiners of each person, not in order to confirm what was done, but in order that they might receive an overturning of the wonder from somewhere and, having constructed some false pretense, might overturn the believing crowd by a rush. Oh, the excess of wickedness!

7.8.4 To fight against the truth and not to worship the one doing these things, but to drag through the dirt the benefactor; not to marvel at the power, but to disparage by trying the matters. Be persuaded even by the parents, O Pharisees, that the man was born with the blindness; and yet again you run back to the blind man, from the second and third, being informed by him of the evil attempts and the plots.

7.8.5 But whenever you fall from the first trial, you move to the second; whenever from the second, to the third; whenever from the third, to the next. As a fox is running through paths, and everywhere you are surrounded by the nets of the truth; but the exit from the wonder is without escape. However, not of all...

You are weaving a web of deceit, making it colorful indeed, but attacking weakly and without permanence. This sickness is your inheritance. You are children like unbelieving fathers. Such were they also in their manner regarding the wonders in Egypt. They were being saved from wars in a new way, yet they disbelieved the one giving salvation even though they were saved by hope. They were being fed with foods surpassing nature, and among those who were starving, they were even more ungrateful; they received manna sent from heaven, and they even craved the stench of the Egyptian leeks and onions. They were shaded during the day by a pillar of cloud so that they would not be afflicted by the heat of the solar ray, and in the night they seized a pillar of fire, having taken another new luminary distinct from the moon, and as if enjoying no divine energy, they thus sought new and celestial gods, profiting from them, so that Moses, having been detained a little on the mountain in the giving of the law, might draw them back to the return.

You truly are heirs of that ignorance, not having loved the law and hating the grace, needing not a rod of carob for supervision, but an iron one. You see a man who has passed into light, yet has remained inactive in his senses until far into his age, being led by alien eyes, sitting daily before the temple, practicing the craft of misfortune so that he might draw many into pity, the city having a witness to the suffering, seeing now and being healed quickly, not by various medicinal compositions, nor by iron cuts, but by clay alone, and this happening through saliva.

And how have you not been placed, not been struck with amazement, not casting down to the earth, worshiping the one who created the eyes from the earth, and respecting the divine energy? Instead, you are bursting with envy and you pursue God as a rival craftsman, as creators pursuing a creator, as those of the same kind pursuing the one of the same kind. And encountering old books, how many were written during the economy of the people, and how many clearly teach the reigns of kings and the history concerning them, receive the things said about each one with obedience, as some consider Moses to be a small god and exult over Elisha and his teacher...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
